citation: Lewis Presser, A., Vahey, P., & Dominguez, X. (2015). Improving mathematics learning by integrating curricular activities with innovative and developmentally appropriate digital apps: Findings from the Next Generation Preschool Math evaluation. Paper presented at the Society for Research on Educational Effectiveness (SREE) Spring 2015 Conference, Washington, DC. ERIC ED562305.
report_number: ERIC ED562305 (SREE Spring 2015 Conference abstract/paper); OpenAlex W2336420480; no journal DOI. Next Generation Preschool Math (NGPM), NSF DRL-1119118 (EDC / SRI International).
design: Blocked cluster-randomized design (BRD); assignment level = classroom/center (School in registry); 16 early-childhood centers (one classroom/teacher each) in NYC and San Francisco serving >=50% low-income children, blocked into 8 pairs and randomized within block to NGPM (TPD + supplemental tablet-augmented math curriculum) vs business-as-usual control; ~8-10 children individually assessed per class, n=169 children total (3.6% post-test attrition). Subject = mathematics (subitizing, equipartitioning); grade = Pre-K. Students nested within classrooms nested within blocks; impact estimated with 2-level HLM controlling for classroom-level pretest.
problems: Conference paper (SREE 2015 abstract, 4-page body + appendices) rather than a full journal report, so reporting is limited. Only ONE numeric achievement effect size is given: the RQ1 confirmatory contrast on the NGPM unit-specific (developer-made) assessment, reported as 'effect size=.51' (p=.026), with adjusted post-test means M_t=59.69, M_c=53.53 (classroom-level pretest controlled, 2-level HLM). The paper does NOT report: the impact coefficient's standard error, per-group SDs, per-condition n, which SD standardized the .51, whether .51 is already small-sample (Hedges) corrected, or the design-effect ICC -- so g_var/g_se cannot be computed and g is taken as the reported ES (~0.51). For the exploratory outcomes the paper gives only significance verdicts and NO numbers: RQ3 subitizing subscale = significant; RQ4 equipartitioning subscale = approached significance; RQ5 general math knowledge on the REMA (Research-based Early Math Assessment; standardized/independent, distal) = NOT statistically significant. The REMA contrast (the independent-measure outcome the meta-analysis would prefer) is therefore recorded as a row with null statistics. NOTE: this 2015 SREE paper is distinct from the later Lewis Presser et al. 2020 journal article (ECRQ, 'The impact of a supplementary preschool mathematics curriculum on children's early mathematics learning'); the registry short-name 'Lewis Presser et al. 2015' and prek/Low-SES/'TPD for curricula'/Res-Dev/School-RCT/Short codings match this SREE conference paper.

effect_sizes.arm_label: NGPM (TPD + supplemental tablet math curriculum) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: NGPM unit-specific mathematics assessment (subitizing + equipartitioning; developer-made battery, flipbook + manipulatives, IRT-scaled, reliability .75 pre / .76 post)
effect_sizes.g_method: Reported standardized effect size taken directly: 'effect size=.51' for the RQ1 confirmatory NGPM-vs-control contrast on the unit-specific assessment, from a 2-level HLM (students nested in classrooms) with classroom-level pretest as covariate (p=.026; adjusted post-test M_t=59.69, M_c=53.53). The paper does not state the standardizing SD or whether a small-sample (Hedges J) correction was applied; g recorded as the reported value. Cannot recompute from means (no SDs reported); cannot compute Var(g)/SE (no impact SE, no per-group SD or n disclosed).
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.4 (Findings, RQ1); Appendix B Figure/Table 1 (line graph of adjusted means)
effect_sizes.notes: Headline confirmatory outcome. Developer-made, proximal/unit-specific measure (NOT an independent test), so likely excluded by the meta-analysis's independent-measure criterion but extracted per spec (central filtering). Component subscales reported only as significance verdicts (RQ3 subitizing significant; RQ4 equipartitioning approached significance) with no numeric effect sizes, so they are not extracted as separate rows. cluster_adjusted=true because .51 comes from the multilevel HLM accounting for classroom nesting; n_clusters=16 centers; ICC not reported (left null, not guessed).

effect_sizes.arm_label: NGPM (TPD + supplemental tablet math curriculum) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: REMA (Research-based Early Mathematics Assessment; Clements & Sarama) -- general/distal mathematics knowledge
effect_sizes.g_method: Not computable: the paper reports only a significance verdict for the RQ5 REMA contrast ('did not differ significantly on general mathematics knowledge'), with no means, SDs, n, impact coefficient, SE, or effect size.
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.4 (Exploratory RQs / RQ5); Data Collection (REMA described p.3-4)
effect_sizes.notes: This is the INDEPENDENT/standardized distal achievement measure the Visscher et al. meta-analysis would prefer. Analyzed via 2-level HLM (RQ5). Result reported as non-significant only; no numeric statistics given, so g and variance cannot be derived. Recorded for completeness so the missing independent-measure effect is traceable. If author/full data become available, this is the contrast to populate.
